question: According to Census of India 2011, female adolescents in the age group of 10-19 years had a share of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**20.9%**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, the female population in the age group of 10-19 years had a share of 20.9%.
 
• This percentage is significant as it represents nearly half of the adolescent population within this age group.
 
• The data highlights the gender distribution among adolescents, which is crucial for planning and implementing youth-centric policies.
 
• Understanding the demographic distribution helps in addressing the specific needs of female adolescents in terms of education, health, and social services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India 2011:**

 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872 and the 7th after independence.
 
• It collects demographic data that includes various parameters such as population size, distribution, density, sex ratio, and literacy rate.
 
• The data collected is crucial for policy-making, planning, and administration at all levels of government.
 
 
 
• **Adolescent Age Group (10-19 years):**
 
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) defines adolescents as individuals in the 10 to 19 years age group.
 
• This stage marks the transition from childhood to adulthood and is characterized by significant physical, psychological, and social changes.
 
• Adolescents require special attention in terms of health, education, and social support to ensure their overall development.
 
• Policies targeting adolescents aim to address issues like reproductive health, substance abuse, and mental health.
 
 
 
• **Female Adolescents:**
 
 
• Female adolescents face unique challenges such as gender-based discrimination, early marriage, and limited access to education and healthcare.
 
• Empowering female adolescents through education and health initiatives is crucial for their personal development and for achieving gender equality.
 
• Programs like the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (Save the Daughter, Educate the Daughter) aim to improve the status of girls in society by promoting education and protection.
